assets.alt: A proxy or manager agent exchanges work with product, developer, and QA agents, which can also communicate directly with one another before a report is produced.
assets.caption: In collaboration, team agents can communicate laterally while a manager remains the user-facing entry point.

assets.alt: Three agent communication patterns: direct message passing, shared conversational memory with handoff control, and agents exposed as MCP tools to an orchestrator.
assets.caption: Agents can coordinate through explicit messages, shared state, or tool-style calls with different visibility and control trade-offs.

assets.alt: Agent evaluation ecosystem connecting red-team tests, critics, grounding, benchmarks, users, a feedback store, and a monitoring agent to the primary agent.
assets.caption: Reliable agents combine internal feedback with red-team, grounding, benchmark, human, and operational evaluation signals.

assets.alt: Sequential agent flow in which specialized planning, research, and content agents pass control and information forward to produce a report.
assets.caption: An agent flow assigns each stage to a specialist and passes the evolving task state along a defined sequence.

assets.alt: Research agent workflow with an input guard before tool use and an output guard validating a typed research plan before a filesystem tool writes the output file.
assets.caption: Input and output guardrails validate the agent boundary before tools act and before results leave the workflow.

assets.alt: Five nested agent layers: persona at the core, then tools and actions, reasoning and planning, knowledge and memory, and evaluation and feedback.
assets.caption: Agent capability grows from persona through action, planning, memory, and finally evaluation and feedback.

assets.alt: An orchestration agent delegates to knowledge, video-search, and web-search workers, gathers their outputs, and returns a report through the central orchestrator.
assets.caption: Hub-and-spoke orchestration funnels delegation and result synthesis through one coordinating agent.

assets.alt: Deployment decision tree routing low-latency agents to edge clients, medium-latency work to synchronous or asynchronous APIs, and long jobs to event-driven workers, all connected to tools and telemetry.
assets.caption: Latency and tool requirements determine whether an agent belongs at the edge, behind an API, or in an event-driven worker.

assets.alt: Planning agent exposing internal tools and equivalent external tools through local MCP-stdio and remote MCP-SSE servers, with JSON tool descriptions sent to the LLM.
assets.caption: The same tool contract can be implemented in-process, on a local MCP server, or on a remote MCP server.

assets.alt: Decision tree reading workspace signals and routing by complexity, task phase, stagnation, contradiction, knowledge gap, completion, or low confidence to response, planning, memory, evaluation, or escalation modules.
assets.caption: Attention routing converts workspace signals into the next cognitive module, including escalation when confidence is too low.

assets.alt: A cognitive cycle executes a module, updates workspace, evaluates results, and raises signals inside an outer agentic loop that controls iterations, convergence, and budget limits.
assets.caption: The inner cognitive cycle selects and evaluates steps; the outer agentic loop controls continuation, convergence, and budgets.

assets.alt: Cognitive agent architecture linking perception, memory, attention, planning, execution, evaluation, a shared workspace, and a confidence gate that can respond, continue, replan, or escalate.
assets.caption: A shared cognitive workspace lets perception, memory, planning, execution, and evaluation coordinate through explicit state.

assets.alt: Mapping from agent failure modes to cognitive deficits and architecture fixes: wrong answers to evaluation, loops to attention, rigid plans to replanning, overconfidence to confidence gating, and shallow composition to perception.
assets.caption: Each recurring failure mode points to a missing cognitive capability and a corresponding architectural control.

assets.alt: Collaborative agent loop where a turn manager selects researcher, critic, or synthesizer agents, each contributes to shared state, and the process rotates until a consensus check produces final synthesis.
assets.caption: A collaboration loop rotates contributors and critics over shared state until the team reaches a synthesis threshold.

assets.alt: Four multi-agent coordination layouts: sequential handoff, parallel delegation, hierarchical coordination, and an iterative generate-critique-refine loop.
assets.caption: Sequential, parallel, hierarchical, and iterative coordination patterns fit different task dependencies and review needs.

assets.alt: Customer-support flow from triage through retrieval and grounding, optional scoped API action with guardrails, answer composition, feedback logging, or handoff to a human.
assets.caption: A production support agent separates triage, evidence retrieval, grounding, guarded actions, response composition, and human escalation.

assets.alt: Deep-research state machine that initializes a plan, connects search tools, iterates through questions, updates findings and the plan, checks goal completion, and sends results to a synthesis agent.
assets.caption: Deep research externalizes questions, findings, and plan state so the loop can stop, replan, or synthesize deliberately.

assets.alt: Research planner orchestrating web-search, extraction, and analysis workers, with a critic returning gaps and a writer producing a cited final report.
assets.caption: A deep-research system separates evidence gathering, analysis, critique, gap filling, and cited synthesis.

assets.alt: Comparison of grounding, critic, and evaluation agents: grounding checks an answer against retrieved context, a critic applies a rubric and feedback, and an evaluator assigns a score or assessment.
assets.caption: Grounders verify evidence, critics drive revision, and evaluators grade outputs without necessarily blocking them.

assets.alt: A user-facing front-door orchestrator routes work through APIs, MCP services, or an event hub to microservice agents and scalable long-running worker agents.
assets.caption: A front-door agent can route interactive work to services and long-running work to a scalable event-driven worker pool.

assets.alt: Simple and expanded memory graphs representing Back to the Future entities such as people, places, and items with typed relationships including mentored_by, child_of, and located_in.
assets.caption: Graph memory preserves entities, attributes, and typed relationships that flat conversation history cannot express directly.

assets.alt: RAG agent receives context from a knowledge store and sends its answer plus the same context to a grounding agent, which returns a final answer or feedback.
assets.caption: A grounding agent checks the generated answer against the exact evidence used by the RAG agent.

assets.alt: Comparison of a shared conversational flow, a controlled pass-off flow, and a guarded handoff flow with filtered context and input-output checks between agents.
assets.caption: Handoffs differ in how much conversation state moves forward and where control and guardrails are applied.

assets.alt: MCP tools and resources mapped across agent layers: application APIs for persona, tools and workflows for action and planning, data stores for memory, and evaluation tools for feedback.
assets.caption: MCP can support every functional agent layer, not only direct tool execution.

assets.alt: MCP architecture where AI agents, LLM applications, desktop clients, and editors connect through an MCP client and JSON-RPC transport to servers wrapping files, databases, web APIs, and other agents.
assets.caption: MCP standardizes how many client types discover and invoke services across local and remote transports.

assets.alt: MCP server exposing three capability groups: prompt templates, data resources such as files and databases, and actionable tools such as search, email, database queries, and agent invocation.
assets.caption: MCP distinguishes reusable prompt templates, readable resources, and callable tools.

assets.alt: An agent calls list_tools on a search MCP server, receives JSON tool descriptions, then invokes a web-search tool over local stdio or remote HTTP transport.
assets.caption: MCP tool discovery gives an agent machine-readable schemas before it chooses and invokes a tool.

assets.alt: Memory-compression pipeline clustering repetitive time-travel preferences, summarizing them into consolidated knowledge, embedding the summary, and storing it in a vector database.
assets.caption: Memory compression turns redundant observations into a compact, retrievable summary instead of storing every repetition.

assets.alt: Memory taxonomy dividing sensory, short-term, and long-term memory; long-term memory further branches into explicit episodic and semantic memory and implicit procedural memory.
assets.caption: Agents most often model conversational short-term memory and explicit long-term episodic or semantic memory.

assets.alt: Comparison of one agent using three MCP tool servers with a three-agent flow in which research, planning, and filesystem agents each own one tool set and pass work sequentially.
assets.caption: Splitting a monolithic agent into specialists narrows each role, tool set, and handoff contract.

assets.alt: Orchestrator loop that decomposes a complex goal, tracks subtask state, delegates pending work to a worker, evaluates results, replans when needed, and synthesizes final output.
assets.caption: The orchestrator owns plan and state, while worker agents execute bounded subtasks and return results for evaluation.

assets.alt: RAG, research, and support agents sending traces to Phoenix for monitoring, token cost, latency, session metadata, experiments, and custom or agent evaluators.
assets.caption: Phoenix centralizes agent traces, costs, latency, session metadata, experiments, and evaluation results.

assets.alt: Sequence diagram where an LLM alternates thought, tool action, and observation until it reaches the goal and returns a final answer to the user.
assets.caption: ReAct interleaves reasoning with tool actions and observations until the agent can answer or must continue.

assets.alt: Reflexion flow from an initial attempt through evaluation and critique; failed attempts generate a reflection stored in context and guide retries until success or a maximum-iteration limit.
assets.caption: Reflexion converts evaluation feedback into remembered guidance for the next attempt, bounded by a retry limit.

assets.alt: Two-part memory workflow: conversations are distilled into preference facts and embedded in a vector database; later queries retrieve those facts and add them to the LLM prompt.
assets.caption: Semantic memory stores distilled facts, then retrieves the relevant ones to augment a later prompt.

assets.alt: Sense-Plan-Act-Learn cycle illustrated by a travel agent that receives a booking goal, plans tasks, calls a flight tool, observes failure, and revises the plan.
assets.caption: The SPAL cycle turns tool feedback into a revised plan instead of treating execution as a one-shot action.

assets.alt: Comparison of short-horizon goals handled by an internal sense-plan-act-learn loop and long-horizon goals handled by an external decide-plan-tool-state loop.
assets.caption: Long-horizon work externalizes decisions, state, plans, and tools beyond the agent's internal task loop.

assets.alt: Test-driven agent development cycle of Think, Test, Prompt, and Refactor, with expected and wrong benchmark outputs and an evaluator agent checking results.
assets.caption: Test-driven agent development iterates over goals, evaluations, prompts, tools, and regression checks.

assets.alt: Tree-of-Thought flow branching an initial thought into alternative next steps, evaluating whether a solution is found, and continuing with new branches when needed.
assets.caption: Tree-of-Thought explores and evaluates alternative reasoning branches instead of committing to one linear path.

assets.alt: Comparison of an untyped planning-agent output whose format varies with a typed ResearchPlanModel whose fixed task list can pass directly to an execution agent.
assets.caption: Typed outputs replace fragile free-form handoffs with a schema the next agent can validate and consume directly.
